finding.claim: Unknown-kid tokens force an unthrottled synchronous JWKS refetch on every request (DoS). Medium severity, high confidence.
finding.source: kid header of an unauthenticated token (get_signing_key_from_jwt reads it unverified)
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP fetch in fetch_data via get_signing_keys(refresh=True), default timeout 30s

trace.note: decode_token with verify_signature=False reads header
_validate_headers checks kid is a string only
header.get('kid') passed to get_signing_key
cache miss triggers get_signing_keys(refresh=True)
fetch_data issues urllib request, no negative cache or rate limit

finding.guards_checked: kid must be str (api_jws.py:430-432); cache consulted first but bypassed on miss; lru_cache does not cache exceptions so every unknown kid refetches; no rate limiting or negative caching anywhere on the path

finding.claim: With cache_keys=True, a signing key removed or rotated out of the JWKS keeps verifying tokens until LRU eviction. Low severity, informational; behavior is documented.
finding.source: Any token whose kid previously resolved to a key

trace.note: lru_cache wraps get_signing_key keyed on kid
successful lookups are cached with no time-based expiry
get_signing_key_from_jwt returns cached key without rechecking JWK Set

finding.guards_checked: None on key age or continued presence in JWKS; docstring (jwks_client.py:44-52) states there is no time-based expiration

finding.claim: Signature segment accepts non-canonical base64url (non-validating decoder), so a valid token with junk characters appended to the signature segment verifies. Low severity; token-string malleability. Medium confidence, from reading only, not executed.
finding.source: Attacker holding a valid token appends non-alphabet characters (e.g. 4 x '!') to the signature segment
finding.sink: Signature bytes decoded and compared in alg.verify (api_jws.py:416)

trace.note: base64url_decode(crypto_segment)
base64.urlsafe_b64decode discards non-alphabet chars, so decoded bytes are identical
HMAC/RSA/EC verify passes on identical bytes

finding.guards_checked: Signing input excludes the signature segment, so header and payload are integrity-protected; padding errors caught at api_jws.py:363-364; compare is constant-time on decoded bytes. Only the raw token string differs, so impact requires app-level keying on the token string

finding.claim: Algorithm-confusion guard for HMAC relies on is_pem_format regex that requires newline after BEGIN/END markers; a public key in a non-matching PEM layout (e.g. trailing spaces) may be accepted as an HMAC secret. Low severity; unverified: depends on whether OpenSSL/cryptography loads that layout.
finding.source: Token header alg=HS256 (api_jws.py:382), precondition: application allows HS* alongside RS*/ES* with the same public key bytes
finding.sink: HMACAlgorithm.sign/verify uses server public-key bytes as HMAC secret (algorithms.py:407-411)

trace.note: get_algorithm_by_name(alg) selects HMAC from attacker-chosen header alg
is_pem_format check; returns False for non-matching PEM layout
regex requires \r?\n after BEGIN and before END
JWK-shaped check only catches JSON with kty

finding.guards_checked: Caller-supplied algorithms allow-list (api_jws.py:386-387, documented as required); PEM regex; JWK kty check; HMAC key emptiness check. Whether a non-matching layout loads as a public key was not verified

finding.claim: Claim validators catch only ValueError on int() conversion, so null or Infinity iat/nbf/exp raises TypeError/OverflowError instead of InvalidTokenError. Low severity, hardening; not a bypass.
finding.source: iat/nbf/exp values in a token payload; requires valid signature or verify_signature=False with explicit verify_exp/verify_iat enabled

trace.note: payload decoded after signature check
_validate_iat called when verify_iat
int(payload['iat']) except ValueError only
int(payload['exp']) same pattern

finding.guards_checked: Claim checks run only after signature verification unless verify_signature=False; _merge_options disables verify_* by default when verify_signature=False (api_jwt.py:81-89)

finding.claim: JWKS fetch hardening gaps: scheme is checked only on the initial URI, redirects are followed without re-checking, and the response body is read with no size limit. Low severity; exploitable only if the caller builds uri from untrusted input or the endpoint is compromised.
finding.sink: urllib urlopen and json.load of the response body

trace.note: scheme check on initial URI only
urlopen follows redirects by default
json.load reads unbounded body

finding.guards_checked: http/https scheme check at construction; file:// blocked by urllib redirect handling (not verified); no SSRF protection to internal hosts; no size limit
